title: Nehemiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Nehemiah chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Nehemiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Nehemiah Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The children of Israel were assembled with fasting
The Levites stood up upon the stairs
They read in the book of the law of the LORD
The Levites said, 'Stand up and bless the LORD'
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Israel were assembled with fasting
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:1 states that on the twenty and fourth day of the month, the children of Israel were assembled with fasting, which is the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel put on themselves when they assembled?
questions.correctAnswer: Sackclothes and earth upon them
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:1 says the children of Israel were assembled with fasting, and with sackclothes, and earth upon them.

questions.question: Who did the seed of Israel separate themselves from?
questions.correctAnswer: All strangers
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:2 states the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers.

questions.question: What did the seed of Israel do after separating themselves from strangers?
options: Confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers
questions.correctAnswer: Confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:2 says they stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.

questions.question: How long did they read in the book of the law of the LORD their God?
options: One fourth part of the day
questions.correctAnswer: One fourth part of the day
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:3 states they read in the book of the law of the LORD one fourth part of the day.

questions.question: Who stood up upon the stairs and cried with a loud voice unto the LORD?
options: The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:4 states these Levites stood upon the stairs and cried with a loud voice unto the LORD their God.

questions.question: What did the Levites say to the people in Nehemiah 9:5?
options: Stand up and bless the LORD your God for ever and ever
Sit down and listen to the law
questions.correctAnswer: Stand up and bless the LORD your God for ever and ever
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:5 records the Levites saying, 'Stand up and bless the LORD your God for ever and ever.'

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 9:6, who made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD alone
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:6 says, 'Thou, even thou, art LORD alone; thou hast made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host.'

questions.question: Who did God choose and bring forth out of Ur of the Chaldees?
questions.correctAnswer: Abram
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:7 states, 'Thou art the LORD the God, who didst choose Abram, and broughtest him forth out of Ur of the Chaldees.'

questions.question: What did God give to Abram's seed in the covenant?
options: The land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites
questions.correctAnswer: The land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:8 declares God made a covenant to give the land of these peoples to Abram's seed.

questions.question: What did God do after seeing the affliction of the fathers in Egypt?
options: He heard their cry by the Red sea
He gave them a new law
questions.correctAnswer: He heard their cry by the Red sea
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:9 says God saw the affliction of their fathers in Egypt and heard their cry by the Red sea.

questions.question: True or False: The Levites stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:2 states the seed of Israel stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

questions.question: True or False: God led the children of Israel by a cloudy pillar during the day and a pillar of fire at night.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:12 states God led them in the day by a cloudy pillar and in the night by a pillar of fire.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 9 says that God gave the children of Israel golden idols to worship.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nowhere in Nehemiah 9 does it say God gave golden idols; rather, the chapter focuses on confessing sins and God’s mighty acts.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 9 mentions God divided the sea so the children of Israel could walk on dry land.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:11 states God divided the sea before them so they went through on dry land.

medium.title: Nehemiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Nehemiah Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 9:14, through whose hand did God command the children of Israel precepts, statutes, and laws?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:14 states that God commanded precepts, statutes, and laws by the hand of Moses thy servant.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 9:15 promise will happen if God’s people trust in His provision as described in Nehemiah 9:14?
options: They will possess the land promised to their fathers
They will never face hunger or thirst
They will multiply like the stars
They will be given strong cities
questions.correctAnswer: They will possess the land promised to their fathers
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:15 promises they should go in to possess the land which God had sworn to give them, following the commandments given by Moses in 9:14.

questions.question: What was the response of the people and their fathers to God's commandments as described in Nehemiah 9:16?
options: They dealt proudly and hardened their necks
They divided the land among themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They dealt proudly and hardened their necks
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:16 states that they and their fathers dealt proudly, hardened their necks, and hearkened not to God's commandments.

questions.question: How do Nehemiah 9:16 and 9:17 together explain the people's attitude and God's character?
options: People rebelled and God remained gracious and merciful
People followed God and God punished them
People were obedient and God rewarded them
People were fearful and God abandoned them
questions.correctAnswer: People rebelled and God remained gracious and merciful
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:16-17 show that although the people rebelled and refused to obey, God is ready to pardon, gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and did not forsake them.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 9:18, what sinful act did the Israelites commit despite God’s wonders?
options: They made a molten calf and worshipped it
They refused to enter the promised land
They destroyed the altar of God
questions.correctAnswer: They made a molten calf and worshipped it
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:18 states that the Israelites made a molten calf and said, 'This is thy God that brought thee up out of Egypt,' committing great provocations.

questions.question: What continual presence did God provide for the Israelites in the wilderness as described in Nehemiah 9:19?
options: Pillar of cloud by day and pillar of fire by night
questions.correctAnswer: Pillar of cloud by day and pillar of fire by night
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:19 explains that the pillar of cloud departed not from them by day and the pillar of fire by night to show them the way.

questions.question: How did God sustain the Israelites physically during their 40 years in the wilderness according to Nehemiah 9:20-21?
options: Provided manna, water, and clothing that did not wear out
Sent prophets to teach laws daily
Led them into battles to build strength
questions.correctAnswer: Provided manna, water, and clothing that did not wear out
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:20-21 states God gave manna and water, sustained them for 40 years so they lacked nothing, their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.

questions.question: What territories did God give to Israel as mentioned in Nehemiah 9:22?
options: The lands of Sihon, Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan
questions.correctAnswer: The lands of Sihon, Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:22 specifies that God gave kingdoms and nations, including the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 9:23, what promise did God fulfill for the children of Israel?
options: He multiplied their children as the stars of heaven and brought them into the promised land
He gave them victory over Egypt
He made them rulers over all nations
questions.correctAnswer: He multiplied their children as the stars of heaven and brought them into the promised land
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:23 says God multiplied their children as the stars of heaven and brought them into the land promised to their fathers.

questions.question: What was the nature of the land and possessions the Israelites acquired as described in Nehemiah 9:25?
options: Strong cities, a fat land, houses full of goods, wells, vineyards, and fruit trees
questions.correctAnswer: Strong cities, a fat land, houses full of goods, wells, vineyards, and fruit trees
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:25 describes the land as fat with strong cities, houses full of goods, wells dug, vineyards, oliveyards, and fruit trees in abundance.

questions.question: Despite God's blessings, what did the Israelites do according to Nehemiah 9:26?
options: They were disobedient, rebelled, cast God's law behind their backs, and slew the prophets
They built altars to God everywhere
questions.correctAnswer: They were disobedient, rebelled, cast God's law behind their backs, and slew the prophets
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:26 states they were disobedient and rebelled, cast God's law behind their backs, and slew the prophets who testified against them.

questions.question: How does understanding the repeated rebellion in Nehemiah 9:16-17 and 9:26 encourage practical Christian living today?
options: It encourages humility, repentance, and reliance on God's mercy
It shows that disobedience has no consequences
It suggests ignoring God's commandments is acceptable
It promotes independence from God's guidance
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages humility, repentance, and reliance on God's mercy
questions.explanation: The verses reveal human rebellion but also God's mercy, encouraging believers to live humbly, repent, and depend on God’s grace.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 9:19 indicates that God’s guidance was visible both day and night in the wilderness.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:19 states the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night led the Israelites, showing God's continuous guidance.

questions.question: True or False: According to Nehemiah 9:21, the Israelites' clothes wore out and their feet swelled after wandering in the wilderness for forty years.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:21 explicitly says their clothes did not wax old and their feet did not swell during the 40 years.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 9:17 describes God as one who quickly punishes without forgiveness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:17 describes God as ready to pardon, gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, not quick to punish without forgiveness.

hard.title: Nehemiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Nehemiah Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 9:27, what did God do when the Israelites cried out in their time of trouble?
options: He heard them from heaven and gave them saviours
He ignored their cries and left them in trouble
He sent angels to fight for them
questions.correctAnswer: He heard them from heaven and gave them saviours
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:27 states that God heard them from heaven and according to His manifold mercies gave them saviours who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.

questions.question: What happened after the Israelites had rest, according to Nehemiah 9:28?
options: They did evil again before God
They sent offerings to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They did evil again before God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:28 explains that after the Israelites had rest, they did evil again before God, resulting in God leaving them in the hand of their enemies.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 9:29, how did the Israelites respond to God's testimony against them?
options: They dealt proudly and hearkened not to God's commandments
They repented immediately and followed the law
They built a new covenant altar
questions.correctAnswer: They dealt proudly and hearkened not to God's commandments
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:29 states that the Israelites dealt proudly and hearkened not unto God's commandments but sinned against His judgments.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 9:30, how long did God forbear the Israelites despite their disobedience?
questions.correctAnswer: Many years
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:30 says that God forbear them many years and testified against them by His spirit in His prophets.

questions.question: What reason does Nehemiah 9:31 give for God not utterly consuming the Israelites despite their sins?
options: Because of God's great mercies and being gracious and merciful
Because the priests interceded for them
Because the kings pleaded for them
questions.correctAnswer: Because of God's great mercies and being gracious and merciful
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:31 explains that God did not utterly consume them nor forsake them for His great mercies' sake, as He is gracious and merciful.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 9:38, who sealed the sure covenant made because of the people's distress?
questions.correctAnswer: Princes, Levites, and priests
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:38 states that the princes, Levites, and priests sealed the covenant that was made and written because of the people's suffering.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'sav-iors' (Nehemiah 9:27) most accurately mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverers
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word translated as 'saviours' in Nehemiah 9:27 means 'deliverers,' those who rescue or save from danger or oppression.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Nehemiah 9:27-29 to describe Israel's repeated disobedience and God's mercy?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:27-29 uses parallelism, repeating the cycle of Israel's sin, punishment, crying out, and God's mercy, to emphasize their disobedience and God's patience.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of Israel's repeated disobedience and God's mercy found in Nehemiah 9:30-31?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 31:3
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:3 speaks of God's everlasting love and mercy to Israel despite their failures, echoing Nehemiah 9:30-31 about God's forbearance and mercy.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of God sending saviours according to His mercies as stated in Nehemiah 9:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 2:11
questions.explanation: Luke 2:11 announces the birth of Jesus, the Saviour sent by God, fulfilling the theme in Nehemiah 9:27 of God giving saviours according to His mercies.

questions.question: What precedes the statement in Nehemiah 9:27 about God delivering Israel into the hands of their enemies?
options: God giving the law on Mount Sinai
The crossing of the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: Israel's disobedience and rebellion
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:26 immediately precedes 9:27 and describes Israel's disobedience and rebellion, which leads to their being delivered into the hands of enemies in 9:27.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 9:32 describe God, emphasizing His covenant and mercy?
options: The great, the mighty, and the terrible God
A God who forgets His promises
A God who punishes without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: The great, the mighty, and the terrible God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:32 describes God as great, mighty, and terrible, who keeps covenant and mercy, highlighting His power and faithfulness.

questions.question: What literary feature is used in Nehemiah 9:27-38 that frames the confession and covenant renewal in the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The passage Nehemiah 9:27-38 uses inclusio, a literary framing device, beginning and ending with Israel's disobedience, God's mercy, and their covenant renewal.

questions.question: Which historical context is vital for understanding the distress mentioned in Nehemiah 9:37?
options: Israel's subjugation under foreign kings due to their sins
questions.correctAnswer: Israel's subjugation under foreign kings due to their sins
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:37 mentions distress under kings set over them because of their sins, reflecting Israel's historical subjugation to foreign powers as punishment.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 9:33 states that God is unjust in what is brought upon Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:33 states that God is just in all that is brought upon Israel; He has done right, but Israel has done wickedly.

theological.title: Nehemiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Nehemiah Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Nehemiah 9:17 teach about God's nature in relation to human sin and repentance?
options: God is ready to pardon and is merciful despite human rebellion
God punishes immediately without offering forgiveness
God condones sin if people repent later
God ignores the sin of His people
questions.correctAnswer: God is ready to pardon and is merciful despite human rebellion
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:17 highlights that although Israel rebelled and appointed a captain to return to bondage, God is ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, showing His readiness to forgive despite sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine covenant faithfulness is taught in Nehemiah 9:8?
options: God is righteous and faithfully performs His covenant promises
God breaks His promises when His people fail
God's promises depend solely on human performance
God's covenant is conditional without guarantee
questions.correctAnswer: God is righteous and faithfully performs His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:8 affirms that God made a covenant with Abraham and has performed His words, demonstrating God's righteousness and unwavering covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin and its consequences is taught in Nehemiah 9:26?
options: Disobedience leads to rejection of God's law and persecution of His prophets
Sin has no real consequences for the covenant people
God condones the killing of prophets
Rebellion is irrelevant to covenant relationship
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience leads to rejection of God's law and persecution of His prophets
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:26 shows that the people's disobedience caused them to cast God's law behind their backs and to kill the prophets sent to turn them back, indicating the serious consequences of sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Nehemiah 9:31 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:31 states that God did not utterly consume or forsake His people because of His great mercies, clearly demonstrating the attribute of divine mercy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly exemplified in Nehemiah 9:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:6 declares that the LORD alone made the heavens and the earth and preserves all things, emphasizing God's sovereignty over creation.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 9:13-14 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine revelation and law?
options: It underscores God's revelation through the giving of laws and commandments on Sinai
It denies the importance of the Mosaic Law for Israel
It replaces the Law with new commandments
It emphasizes human tradition over divine law
questions.correctAnswer: It underscores God's revelation through the giving of laws and commandments on Sinai
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 describe God speaking from heaven on Sinai and giving right judgments, statutes, and commandments through Moses, linking to the biblical theme of God’s self-revelation through the Law.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared by Nehemiah 9:9-11 regarding God's deliverance?
options: God's power to save His people from bondage prefigures ultimate salvation in Christ
God only saves physically, not spiritually
Deliverance from Egypt is the final act of salvation history
God's saving acts are limited to Israel's history
questions.correctAnswer: God's power to save His people from bondage prefigures ultimate salvation in Christ
questions.explanation: The description of God delivering Israel through the Red Sea in verses 9-11 anticipates the greater salvation through Christ, a key redemptive-historical theme.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 9:16 and 9:30 teach about human sin and divine patience?
options: Despite persistent human rebellion, God patiently testifies and withholds immediate judgment
God immediately punishes every sin without any patience
Human sin is inconsequential to God’s judgment
God's patience encourages continual sin without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Despite persistent human rebellion, God patiently testifies and withholds immediate judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 16 and 30 describe Israel's proud rebellion and God's many years of forbearing and testifying against them through His Spirit, showing divine patience despite sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God's covenant faithfulness and human responsibility is taught in Nehemiah 9:29 and 9:33?
options: God is just in judgment and faithful in covenant, but humans are responsible for sinful disobedience
God is unjust and breaks His covenant
Humans are not responsible for sin because God controls all
God overlooks sin to maintain covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God is just in judgment and faithful in covenant, but humans are responsible for sinful disobedience
questions.explanation: Verses 29 and 33 affirm God's justice and covenant faithfulness while also acknowledging that Israel and their leaders acted wickedly and disobeyed God's commandments.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God's providential protection and provision is taught in Nehemiah 9:15 and 9:21?
options: God sustains and provides for His people in the wilderness despite their circumstances
God abandons His people during hardship
Provision is solely the result of human effort
God’s provision is temporary and unreliable
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains and provides for His people in the wilderness despite their circumstances
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 21 show God giving bread from heaven, water from the rock, and sustaining Israel for 40 years so that they lacked nothing, highlighting divine providence.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Nehemiah 9:31-32 teaches God is indifferent to His people's suffering due to their sin. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God is gracious and merciful, and He is deeply aware and just regarding their troubles
God ignores the people's distress because they deserve it
God punishes without hope of restoration
God is unaware of human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God is gracious and merciful, and He is deeply aware and just regarding their troubles
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:31-32 states that God did not utterly consume Israel because of His mercy and acknowledges their troubles as just, showing God’s justice, mercy, and attentiveness to suffering.

questions.question: What doctrine does Nehemiah 9:19 teach about the guidance of the Holy Spirit in Israel's wilderness journey?
options: God's Spirit provided continual guidance and presence during Israel's wandering
God abandoned Israel after the golden calf incident
Israel's guidance was solely by human effort
The Spirit was only given after the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: God's Spirit provided continual guidance and presence during Israel's wandering
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:19 explains that God did not forsake Israel in the wilderness; the pillar of cloud and fire continued to lead them, indicating the Spirit's continual guidance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Nehemiah 9:10 in God's actions against Pharaoh and Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:10 describes God showing signs and wonders on Pharaoh and Egypt because they dealt proudly against Israel, demonstrating God's attribute of justice.

questions.question: What theological significance does Nehemiah 9:38 hold in the covenant renewal context of the post-exilic community?
options: It shows the community's commitment to a renewed covenant sealed by leaders
It indicates rejection of the Mosaic covenant
It shows a casual approach to covenant obligations
It replaces the old covenant with a new one without leaders' involvement
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the community's commitment to a renewed covenant sealed by leaders
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 9:38 records that the people made a sure covenant and had it sealed by princes, Levites, and priests, indicating a solemn and communal commitment to covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by Nehemiah 9:22 and 9:24 about God's granting of land and victory to Israel?
options: God sovereignly gives land and subdues enemies for His covenant people
Israel conquers land through military might alone
God's promises of land are conditional on perfect obedience
The land was possessed by Israel without divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly gives land and subdues enemies for His covenant people
questions.explanation: Verses 22 and 24 describe God giving kingdoms and nations to Israel and subduing the inhabitants, showing His sovereign role in Israel's possession of the promised land.
